subject: Richard Avedon
title: Who was Richard Avedon? The photographer in Ron Howard's Netflix film
answer: Richard Avedon (1923-2004) was an American fashion and portrait photographer who shot for Harper's Bazaar and Vogue and became The New Yorker's first staff photographer in 1992. He is the subject of "Avedon," a documentary directed by Ron Howard that arrives on Netflix on Wednesday, Nov. 11, 2026.
body:
Avedon was born in New York City on May 15, 1923, and died on Oct. 1, 2004, in San Antonio, Texas, while on assignment for The New Yorker. He joined Harper's Bazaar in 1944, moved to Vogue in 1965 and shot most of its covers from 1973 until 1988. His best-known images include "Dovima with Elephants" (1955), a print of which sold for a record £719,000 at Christie's in 2010, and "In the American West" (1985), a book of large-format portraits of working-class Americans. The photographer played by Fred Astaire in the 1957 film "Funny Face" was a fictionalized version of him.

The Netflix documentary, which premiered at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival, runs 1 hour 44 minutes and draws on Avedon's personal archives, including unseen stills and behind-the-scenes footage. It was made by Imagine Documentaries and Fifth Season in association with the Richard Avedon Foundation, with Brian Grazer and Ron Howard among the producers.
in_the_news: Ron Howard's documentary "Avedon" premieres on Netflix on Nov. 11, 2026.
